items.claim: The path override is now gated only on a request header (`x-vercel-isr: 1`), and the same entrypoint is bundled into the non-ISR `_render` function, so a spoofed header re-opens the override that #15959 closed.
items.consequence: Confirmed in-process on the built `_render` handler: `GET /api/public?x_astro_path=/api/private` with header `x-vercel-isr: 1` returns `{"id":"private"}`. If Vercel does not strip this header from client requests (not checkable here), any client can make `_render` serve a different route than the one Vercel's routing, firewall or path rules matched. The existing path-override-security tests still pass because they never send the header. Gate on something the client cannot set, such as a build-time flag for the `_isr` function.

items.claim: The `_isr` function trusts any `x_astro_path` value, so requesting `/_isr?x_astro_path=<route>` directly renders and caches arbitrary routes, including `isr.exclude` routes and ones meant to go through edge middleware.
items.consequence: Confirmed in-process on the isr fixture's `_isr` handler with the ISR header set: `/_isr?x_astro_path=/two` (excluded) returns the Two page and `/_isr?x_astro_path=/api/foo` (excluded by `/^\/api/`) returns `OK foo`. On Vercel the platform would set the header itself for a direct `/_isr` hit, so no spoofing is needed. Excluded routes that the build routes to `_middleware` would be rendered without the middleware, and a personalised response could be stored in the ISR cache under a URL an attacker can re-fetch. The resolved route is never checked against the ISR-eligible set.

items.claim: `url.pathname = realPath` percent-encodes `?`, so the middleware branch (whose header value is path plus query) 404s for any request with a query string; the PR rewrites this block and leaves the bug in place.
items.consequence: Confirmed in-process on the middleware-with-edge-file fixture with `fetch` stubbed to the built `_render` handler: `/` returns 200, but `/?a=1` sends `x-astro-path: /?a=1`, the pathname becomes `/%3Fa=1`, and the response is 404. The query string is also lost. Parse the override with `new URL(realPath, url)` and assign pathname and search separately.

items.claim: `searchParams.get()` form-decodes the ISR path, so paths containing `&`, `+`, `%2F`, `%26` or `%2B` resolve to a different route or different params than the same path served directly.
items.consequence: Confirmed in-process, direct versus via `x_astro_path`: `/api/a+b` gives id `a+b` versus `a b`; `/api/a&b` gives `a&b` versus `a` (truncated at `&`); `/api/a%2Fb` gives 200 versus 404; `/api/a%26b` gives `a%26b` versus `a&b`. How Vercel encodes `$0` when substituting it into the dest could not be checked here, but if it is inserted raw, an ISR dynamic route renders and caches the wrong content for such slugs.

items.claim: Only the pathname is rewritten for ISR requests; the internal `x_astro_path` parameter stays in the URL passed to `app.render`.
items.consequence: By reading the code: for `/one` served via ISR, `Astro.url.href` is `https://site/one?x_astro_path=%2Fone`. Canonical or og:url tags, redirects and pagination links built from `Astro.url` embed the internal parameter, and user code reading `Astro.url.searchParams` sees a key it never sent. The fix is to `url.searchParams.delete(ASTRO_PATH_PARAM)` before rebuilding the request.

items.claim: The fix depends on a hard-coded, undocumented platform header (`x-vercel-isr`) being present with the exact value `'1'` on every ISR invocation.
items.consequence: If Vercel omits or changes the header for some invocation type (for example on-demand revalidation via `x-prerender-revalidate` with the bypass token, background regeneration, or a future platform change), `realPath` stays undefined, the app matches `/_isr`, and a 404 is rendered and cached for the page. That is the same outage this PR fixes, and it would fail silently. The literal is also inline rather than a named constant next to `ASTRO_PATH_PARAM` in `index.ts`.

items.claim: No test covers the restored ISR rewrite or its trust boundary, although the missing handler-level ISR test is why #15959 broke ISR unnoticed.
items.consequence: `test/isr.test.js` only asserts the generated config and routes, and `path-override-security.test.js` only covers requests without `x-vercel-isr`. A future change to this branch can again 404 every ISR page, or widen the override, with CI green. A test that calls the built `_isr` handler with `x_astro_path=/one` (expect the One page) and `_render` with header plus param (expect no override) would pin both.

items.claim: The new block is unformatted and loosely typed: `if(` without a space, a missing semicolon on line 23, and `let realPath = undefined` with no type annotation.
items.consequence: The repo's Biome formatter will rewrite these lines (the history shows follow-up `[ci] format` commits). `realPath` loses the explicit `string | null` type the previous `const` had and relies on control-flow inference; `let realPath: string | null = null;` keeps the old contract.

items.claim: The changeset text "Fix vercel ISR path rewrite" does not describe the user-visible bug.
items.consequence: Users reading the `@astrojs/vercel` changelog cannot tell that this release fixes every ISR-served page returning 404 since the previous patch. Something like "Fixes a regression where pages served through ISR returned a 404" would say so.
